$comment: A verbatim copy of terma-desktop shared/fixtures/auth.json: its delegatedGrant section and tokenRequests.delegated. terma-cli does not read the desktop's fixtures, so copy both again whenever they change there. grant_input.json beside it holds the CLI's own cases for what it reads on stdin.

delegatedGrant.$comment: terma setup -y --env <env> --harness <agents> --org <id> --team <id> --desktop-grant. The app writes in1 (the desktop's identity: ids, no secret) and reads the first stdout line. {"reused":true}: the CLI kept a sign-in for the same user and organization; the app closes stdin. {"challenge","label"}: the app calls delegate with that challenge and label, writes in2 with the code, and closes stdin. Every later stdout line is setup's own output, shown as usual. A first line that is neither (or a challenge that is not 43 base64url characters) fails the run, and so does a second request. When the app has no code to give it closes stdin; the CLI then exits 1 with {"error":{"code":"grant_no_code"}}. The challenge and the code are never shown. terma-cli copies these cases.

cases.name: a stored sign-in for the same user and organization
keys in another order, and a space
setup's output before the request is malformed
a challenge that is not 43 base64url characters
a challenge with a character outside base64url

runs.name: a grant: the code goes in, the run carries on, nothing secret is shown
a reuse: no delegate, stdin closed after the identity
a second request fails the run
a malformed first line fails the run
no code to give: stdin closes, and the CLI exits 1 with grant_no_code

delegated.$comment: Sent by terma-cli alone, with the code the desktop wrote to its stdin and its own verifier: redirect_port 0. The auth host decides from its own record of the code that it is delegated; a delegated code with any other port, and a browser code with port 0, are refused. The desktop never sends this.
